name: Jumjum
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Jumjum Dictionary, trial edition, August 2020 (SIL / Sudan Workshop Programme; compiler T. Stirtz per PDF metadata). 40 pp.
Gilley, Leoma G. 2004. The Lwoian family. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 165-174 (in OPSL 9, SIL-Sudan).
sources.note: Jumjum appears only in the orthographic symbol table; the stress remarks in this volume concern Shilluk (stressed 1pl-inclusive -a suffix) and Dinka/Nuer, not Jumjum.

sources.citation: Andersen, Torben. 2004. Jumjum phonology. Studies in African Linguistics 33(2): 133-162. doi:10.32473/sal.v33i2.107333
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online (also: harvard online access (harvardkey))
sources.note: Nothing: the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur. Covers syllable structure, vowels/harmony, consonants, and tone (sec. 5, p.150: 'Jumjum is a tone language with two underlying tones: high (H) and low (L)'), with three tonal processes (Utterance-final Lowering, Downstepped Raising, Fall Simplification). Dialect described: Watkey.

sources.citation: Fadul, Yousif Aljuzuli et al. 2020 [2016]. Jumjum Consonant and Vowel Book. Trial edition. Kampala: DLPI & Sudan Workshop Programme. 47 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: syllables introduced as 'beats' (p.5); vowels short/long, [ATR] 'heavy/light', High vs Low tone minimal pair kul/kul (p.19); the 'Tone' section (p.31) is an explicit placeholder: '[This section should be completed after further study of tone is done in the Jumjum.]'. No stress statement.

sources.citation: Fadul, Yousif Aljuzuli; Chol, Terafi Mohadin; Teebu, Muusa Nuer; Yousif, Bal Douwash; Blang, Abrahama Kidir; Anur, Abdalmajid Juma. 2020 [1st trial ed. 2016]. Jumjum Grammar Book. sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent; 'Spelling rules' section only; tone mentioned incidentally (dependent verbs long final vowel with falling tone vs short with low tone; glossary defines High/Low tone).
